title: Clique partitions of chordal graphs: quantitative stability and sharp eventual bounds
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the chordal results of the author's preprint "Clique partitions with rooted simplicial defect: quantitative stability and sharp eventual bounds" (Erdős #81 series, Paper IV). With M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋: there is b such that every chordal graph on n vertices has a clique partition into pieces of order at most four with at most M(n) + b pieces (Theorem A); for n large every chordal graph on n vertices has one with at most M(n) pieces, and some chordal graph on n vertices has one with exactly M(n) pieces that is optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem B, the bound asked in Erdős Problem #81 and its sharpness); 1/6 is the least quadratic coefficient (§6.3); the uniform mixed rounding of fractional triangle/K₄ packings (Theorem 3.1); integral stability with explicit constants and edit distance at most 16δ to a complete-split graph, for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn² with γ = 10⁻¹⁶/4 (Theorem 6.1); same-root control of near-optimal partitions: one clique root satisfies all the conclusions of Theorem 6.1 and, for it, every partition with at most M(n) + τ pieces has at most τ + 48δ noncanonical pieces (Corollary 6.1a); the root-defect identity (6.7b); and the eventual classification of the extremal chordal graphs as complete-split graphs with a core of optimal size (Corollary 6.2). Eight statements. The thresholds N are existential; b and N are not claimed optimal.
